html:
A Swedish botanist and doctor who created the system of naming living things still used today. He lived from 1707 to 1778 and taught at Uppsala University.

His Systema Naturae, first printed in 1735, sorted plants, animals and minerals into classes, orders, genera and species. Its later editions, and his Species Plantarum of 1753, gave every species a short two part Latin name, the genus and the species, as in Homo sapiens, a name he coined for humans. Before this, plants often had long descriptive names that differed from book to book.

He sent his students, whom he called apostles, around the world to collect plants. Daniel Solander sailed with James Cook and others went to China, Japan and the Americas. His system made the flood of new species from European voyages manageable, and it set up the work of later naturalists, including Charles Darwin. In 1761 he was made a noble as Carl von Linné.
sum: A Swedish botanist and doctor who created the system of naming living things still used today. He lived from 1707 to 1778 and taught at Uppsala University.
